evals.prompt: /refactor Extract the duplicated validation logic in OrderService and PaymentService into one place
assertions: Runs the full test suite before making any change to establish a baseline
Consolidates the duplicated logic into a single shared function or module and deletes the duplicated copies, rather than adding a new abstraction layer on top of both
The full test suite passes and matches the baseline after each incremental step
No validation or error-handling branch is dropped in the process

evals.prompt: /refactor Extract the discount-calculation block inside calculateOrderTotal (single file, only two call sites) into its own function
assertions: Does not create a formal 6-phase TaskCreate/TaskUpdate chain or spawn parallel Explore subagents for this single-file change with a greppable caller list
Still greps for or otherwise enumerates all callers of calculateOrderTotal before changing it
Runs the existing tests before the change, makes the extraction, and runs tests again afterward
The extracted function preserves the original discount calculation behavior exactly, including any edge case in the original block

evals.prompt: /refactor Rename the legacy UserMgr class to UserManager and update all callers
assertions: Finds all callers via Grep before renaming, including dynamic or string-based references
The old name is fully removed once all callers are migrated, rather than keeping both names indefinitely
Tests pass after each incremental step

evals.prompt: /refactor Rename calculateShipping to computeShippingCost, and while you're in there add a new express-shipping option that charges a $15 surcharge
assertions: Identifies the express-shipping surcharge as new functionality outside refactor's scope, not a structural rename
No express-shipping or surcharge logic is written, edited, or committed during this run
No git commit is created that bundles the new express-shipping behavior together with the rename

The final response either scopes the work to the rename only or explicitly tells the user the express-shipping addition needs a separate implement-feature task, and stops there rather than guessing which the user wants
The sandbox's git history (git log) contains no commit that implements the express-shipping surcharge -- only the rename is committed
The final message to the user explicitly names the express-shipping surcharge as the specific piece that was deferred, not a generic disclaimer
